newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industrials end firmer, golds steady despite Dow's fal.
newsitem.headline: S.African industrials end firmer, golds steady despite Dow's fal.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended stronger in active trade on Tuesday, shaking off some nervousness from Monday's Wall Street's 43-point fall in early trade, dealers said.

They said the U.S. market was perceived to have needed a correction and its effect on the local market had been minimal anyway amid upbeat talk of a cut in South African interest rates in the next six months and a fall in the money market shortage. Dealers said the market had also taken a positive push from Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals who said the bank's net oversold position on its forward book had fallen by one billion dollars by March 31, and was expected to fall further as confidence in the rand increased.
He told Reuters on Tuesday while the central bank was not prepared to comment on the current level of the exchange rate, it welcomed the more stable conditions of the currency over recent months.
The rand was last pegged at 4.4455 bid against the U.S. dollar, while the industrial index added 35.7 points to finish at 8,374.5.

Gold shares started Tuesday unchanged but finished slightly firmer to mixed on the back of bullion's attempts to hold steady and consolidate its small gains around the $341 an ounce level, dealers said.
The gold index went up 5.7 points to close at 1,263.3, with the yellow metal resisting a fall back to last week's $340 trading level.
Dealers said Wall Street's Monday's slide had also dampened industrial futures, while gold contracts heeded bullion's mild up and down rises around the $341 an ounce level.
The June industrial contract closed at 8,210/13 from 8,172 settlement, the golds contract at 885/90 from 891 and the all-share at 6,540/60 from 6,516.
